previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for left upper quadrant abdominal pain worsened by oral and tube feeding intake, different from prior ulcer episodes. After bowel rest and imaging, an EGD revealed a 10 mm gastrojejunal anastomotic ulcer. Initial tube feeding adjustments caused persistent pain, leading to discontinuation and initiation of TPN via PICC on hospital day 7. A small MRSA-positive pustule at the G-tube site was drained and treated. Feeds were retrialed on hospital day 12 with Peptamen Bariatric formula at a cycled rate of 60 mL/hr, which was well tolerated. The PICC was removed, and the patient was discharged home on enteral feeds, liquid pantoprazole twice daily, sucralfate, and an increased nortriptyline dose for pain. Follow-up was arranged with gastroenterology and surgery.

Brief Hospital Course:
The patient presented to our ___ clinic on ___ where 
she was evaluated for abdominal pain and symptoms concerning for 
a recurent gastric ulcer despite high dose oral Protonix and 
Sucralfate. She was admitted to ___ and was started on IV PPI 
BID with Sucralfate and PCA for pain control. A KUB was done 
initially that did not reveal any free abdominal air. She was 
placed on IV fluids and a daily banana bag was given

sent. The patient was found to be low on iron and ferritin (Iron 
25* Nl[30 - 160] ug/dL ; Ferritin 5.0* Nl[13 - 150] ng/mL). Her 
iron suplementation was adjusted. 
 She was then noted to develop some nausea with PCA for which 
she was seen by chronic pain service, and the pain medications 
were adjusted. Narcotics were discontinued due to nausea and dry 
heaving while NPO. Her abdominal pain improved and she tolerated 
a stage 3 diet.

increased from 50mg QHS. Effexor was stopped. The patient's

Discharge Instructions:
Discharge Instructions: 
You were admitted to the Bariatric Surgery Service at ___ 
___ for abdominal pain on ___.

Please call your surgeon or return to the emergency department 
if you develop a fever greater than 101.5, chest pain, shortness 
of breath, severe abdominal pain, pain unrelieved by your pain 
medication, severe nausea or vomiting, severe abdominal 
bloating, inability to eat or drink, foul smelling or colorful 
drainage from your incisions, redness or swelling around your 
incisions, or any other symptoms which are concerning to you.

Diet: Bariatric Stage 3, may advance to stage 4 then 5 as 
tolerated. 
Supplement with cycled gastric tube feeds 60 ml per hour (at a 
rate of 760cc over 12hours daily). Do not drink out of a straw 
or chew gum. 
Medication Instructions:
Resume your home medications, CRUSH ALL PILLS.
You will be starting some new medications:
1.  You are being discharged on medications to treat the pain 
from your operation. These medications will make you drowsy and 
impair your ability to drive a motor vehicle or operate 
machinery safely. You MUST refrain from such activities while 
taking these medications.
2. You should begin taking a chewable complete multivitamin with 
minerals. No gummy vitamins.
3. You should take a stool softener, Colace, twice daily for 
constipation as needed, or until you resume a normal bowel 
pattern.
4. You must not use NSAIDS (non-steroidal anti-inflammatory 
drugs) Examples are Ibuprofen, Motrin, Aleve, Nuprin and 
Naproxen. These agents will cause bleeding and ulcers in your 
digestive system.
Activity:
You may resume exercise at your discretion, no restrictions.

HISTORY:  ___ female status post Roux-en-Y gastric bypass with
abdominal pain.  Evaluation for free air.

COMPARISON:  Comparison is made to abdominal radiograph from ___.

FINDINGS:  Two frontal images of the abdomen demonstrate a normal bowel gas
pattern with moderate fecal load throughout the entire colon.  There is no
pneumatosis or free air.  A gastrostomy tube is seen overlying the mid
abdomen.  A surgical clip is noted in the left upper quadrant.  Visualized
osseous structures are unremarkable.  Multiple phleboliths are seen in the
pelvis.

IMPRESSION:  Normal bowel gas pattern with no evidence of bowel obstruction. 
No free air.
